arxiv-1409-6392.title: Enhanced Pilot-Based Spectrum Sensing Algorithm
arxiv-1409-6392.creator: Ghaith Hattab, Mohammed Ibnkahla
arxiv-1409-6392.description: Abstract In this paper, we develop an enhanced pilot-based spectrum sensing algorithm for cognitive radio. Unlike conventional pilot-based detectors which merely detect the presence of pilot signals, the proposed detector also utilizes the presence of the signal that carries the actual information.

arxiv-1812-02956.title: LNEMLC: Label Network Embeddings for Multi-Label Classification
arxiv-1812-02956.creator: Piotr Szymański, Tomasz Kajdanowicz, and Nitesh V. Chawla
arxiv-1812-02956.description: Abstract Multi-label classification aims to classify instances with discrete non-exclusive labels. Most approaches on multi-label classification focus on effective adaptation or transformation of existing binary and multi-class learning approaches but fail in modelling the joint probability of labels or do not preserve generalization abilities for unseen label combinations.

arxiv-2202-08976.title: MINKOWSKI-TENSOR-BASED SHAPE ANALYSIS METHODS ON THE SPHERE
arxiv-2202-08976.creator: C. COLLISCHON 1, M. KLATT 2, C. RÄTH 3, M. SASAKI 1
arxiv-2202-08976.description: Abstract Recently, Minkowski Tensors (MT) have gained popularity for morphological analysis tasks. As opposed to the scalar Minkowski functionals (MF; in 2D given by area, perimeter and Euler characteristic), MT can characterize symmetry and orientation of a body. This has been used for a variety of tasks, e.g.

arxiv-2303-14502.title: VERN: Vegetation-aware Robot Navigation in Dense Unstructured Outdoor Environments
arxiv-2303-14502.creator: Adarsh Jagan Sathyamoorthy, Kasun Weerakoon, Tianrui Guan, Mason Russell, Damon Conover, Jason Pusey, Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2303-14502.description: Abstract We propose a novel method for autonomous legged robot navigation in densely vegetated environments with a variety of pliable/traversable and non-pliable/untraversable vegetation. We present a novel few-shot learning classifier that can be trained on a few hundred RGB images to differentiate flora that can be navigated through, from the ones that must be circumvented.

arxiv-2405-08814.title: Performance of wave function and Green’s function methods for non-equilibrium many-body dynamics
arxiv-2405-08814.creator: Cian C. Reeves, Gaurav Harsha, Avijit Shee, Yuanran Zhu, Thomas Blommel, Chao Yang, K Birgitta Whaley, Dominika Zgid, Vojtěch Vlček
arxiv-2405-08814.description: Abstract Theoretical descriptions of the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems essentially employ either (i) explicit treatments, relying on the truncation of the expansion of the many-body wavefunction, (ii) compressed representations of the many-body wavefunction, or (iii) evolution of an effective (downfolded) representation through Green’s functions.

arxiv-2406-04822.title: M2NO: Multiresolution Operator Learning with Multiwavelet-based Algebraic Multigrid Method
arxiv-2406-04822.creator: Zhihao Li, Zhilu Lai, Xiaobo Zhang, Wei Wang
arxiv-2406-04822.description: Abstract Solving partial differential equations (PDEs) effectively necessitates a multi-scale approach, particularly critical in high-dimensional scenarios characterized by increasing grid points or resolution. Traditional methods often fail to capture the detailed features necessary for accurate modeling, presenting a significant challenge in scientific computing.

arxiv-2409-01538.title: Investigating early and late-time epochs in f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity
arxiv-2409-01538.creator: Ameya Kolhatkar, Sai Swagat Mishra, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2409-01538.description: Abstract In the following work, a new hybrid model of the form f ⁡ ( Q ) = Q ⁡ ( 1 + a ) + b ​ Q 0 2 Q f(Q)=Q(1+a)+b\frac{Q_{0}^{2}}{Q} has been proposed and confronted using both early as well as late-time constraints.

arxiv-2412-04133.title: Simulating matrix models with tensor networks
arxiv-2412-04133.creator: Enrico M. Brehm, Yibin Guo, Karl Jansen, and Enrico Rinaldi
arxiv-2412-04133.description: Abstract Matrix models, as quantum mechanical systems without explicit spatial dependence, provide valuable insights into higher-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories, especially within the framework of string theory, where they can describe quantum black holes via the holographic principle. Simulating these models allows for exploration of their kinematic and dynamic properties, particularly in parameter regimes that are analytically intractable.

arxiv-2501-03700.title: AuxDepthNet: Real-Time Monocular 3D Object Detection with Depth-Sensitive Features
arxiv-2501-03700.creator: RUOCHEN ZHANG 1, HYEUNG-SIK CHOI 1, DONGWOOK JUNG 1, PHAN HUY NAM ANH 1, SANG-KI JEONG 2, ZIHAO ZHU 1
arxiv-2501-03700.description: Abstract Monocular 3D object detection is a challenging task in autonomous systems due to the lack of explicit depth information in single-view images. Existing methods often depend on external depth estimators or expensive sensors, which increase computational complexity and hinder real-time performance.

arxiv-2508-06108.title: GCHR : Goal-Conditioned Hindsight Regularization for Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2508-06108.creator: Xing Lei, Wenyan Yang, Kaiqiang Ke, Shentao Yang, Xuetao Zhang, Joni Pajarinen, Donglin Wang
arxiv-2508-06108.description: Abstract Goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL) with sparse rewards remains a fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning. While hindsight experience replay (HER) has shown promise by relabeling collected trajectories with achieved goals, we argue that trajectory relabeling alone does not fully exploit the available experiences in off-policy GCRL methods, resulting in limited sample efficiency.

arxiv-2508-19805.title: Separation of Three or More Autonomous Mobile Models under Hierarchical Schedulers Thanks: This research was supported in part by by JSPS KAKENHI No. 25K03079.
arxiv-2508-19805.creator: Shota Naito, Tsukasa Ninomiya, Koichi Wada
arxiv-2508-19805.description: Abstract Understanding the computational power of mobile robot systems is a fundamental challenge in distributed computing. While prior work has focused on pairwise separations between models, we explore how robot capabilities, light observability, and scheduler synchrony interact in more complex ways.

arxiv-2509-01799.title: Optimal information injection and transfer mechanisms for active matter reservoir computing
arxiv-2509-01799.creator: Mario U. Gaimann, Miriam Klopotek
arxiv-2509-01799.description: Abstract Reservoir computing (RC) is a state-of-the-art machine learning method that makes use of the power of dynamical systems (the reservoir) for real-time inference. When using biological complex systems as reservoir substrates, it serves as a testbed for basic questions about bio-inspired computation – of how self-organization generates proper spatiotemporal patterning.

arxiv-2601-12099.title: Large Language Models Struggle with Ethnographic Text Annotation
arxiv-2601-12099.creator: Leonardo S. GoodallCalleva Research CentreOxford Internet InstituteUniversity of Oxford, UK, Dor ShiltonCohn Institute for the History and Philosophy of Science and IdeasTel Aviv University, Israel dorshilt@mail.tau.ac.il Daniel Austin MullinsBirkbeck CollegeUniversity of London, UKCentre for the St
arxiv-2601-12099.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automated text annotation, raising hopes that they might accelerate cross-cultural research by extracting structured data from ethnographic texts. We evaluated 7 state-of-the-art LLMs on their ability to annotate 121 ritual features across 567 ethnographic excerpts. Performance was limited, falling well below levels required for reliable automated annotation.

arxiv-2605-12208.creator: Julian Rodemann julian.rodemann@cispa.de, Alexander Marquard alexander.marquard@campus.lmu.de, Michele Caprio michele.caprio@manchester.ac.uk

arxiv-2605-29963.creator: Mark Vero, Fabian Kaczmarczyck, Ivan Petrov, Ilia Shumailov, Jamie Hayes, Niels Heinen, Tianqi Fan, Luca Invernizzi, Martin Vechev

pmc-10628033.title: Structure and Ecological Function of Fungal Endophytes from Stems of Different Mulberry Cultivars
pmc-10628033.creator: Fangfang Peng, Xunlan Li, Zhaoxin Wei, Youjin Luo, Wu Wang, Guohui Han
pmc-10628033.description: To explore the microbial community structure and ecological function of mulberry and their potential relationship with the resistance of mulberry, the community structure and function of endophytic fungi in 18 mulberry cultivars were analyzed and predicted by using high-throughput sequencing technology and the FUNGuild database.

pmc-10672034.title: Characterization of a Type II L-Asparaginase from the Halotolerant Bacillus subtilis CH11
pmc-10672034.creator: Annsy Arredondo-Nuñez, Gisele Monteiro, Carol N Flores-Fernández, Lina Antenucci, Perttu Permi, Amparo Iris Zavaleta, Martina Aulitto, Giovanni Gallo
pmc-10672034.description: L-asparaginases from bacterial sources have been used in antineoplastic treatments and the food industry. A type II L-asparaginase encoded by the N-truncated gene ansZP21 of halotolerant Bacillus subtilis CH11 isolated from Chilca salterns in Peru was expressed using a heterologous system in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3)pLysS.

pmc-10689861.title: The Impact of Mental Practice on Motor Function in Patients With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
pmc-10689861.creator: Hyun Seok, Yoon-Hee Choi
pmc-10689861.description: Mental practice (MP), the cognitive rehearsal of physical activities without overt movements, has recently emerged as a promising rehabilitation method for patients with stroke. This paper presents a systematic review and meta-analysis critically evaluating the existing evidence to offer a comprehensive estimate of the overall effect of MP on motor function in stroke patients.

pmc-11436204.title: Different Cytotoxicity Induced by Hexabromocyclododecanes on Mouse Neuroblastoma N2a Cells via Oxidative Stress and Mitochondrial Apoptotic Pathway
pmc-11436204.creator: Keyan Wan, Dongting Wu, Guangshan Xie, Yunxiu Li, Jianqing Zhang, Xuetao Wei, Changfu Hao, Wenhui Qiu
pmc-11436204.description: Hexabromocyclododecane (HBCD) is widely used in polystyrene foams, building materials, and electrical equipment as a brominated flame retardant (BFR) and persists in the environment and human body matrix. It has attracted increased attention since its neuroendocrine disorder effects have been observed in humans and animals.

pmc-11617874.title: Effectiveness and safety of acupuncture for carpal tunnel syndrome: An overview of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
pmc-11617874.creator: Yulin Liu, Chao Wang, Qi Wang, Qing Zhang, Songhao Ning, Quanai Zhang
pmc-11617874.description: BackgroundSeveral systematic reviews (SRs) and meta-analyses (MAs) have explored the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), but findings are inconsistent and vary in quality. Therefore, this overview aims to evaluate these SRs and MAs critically, synthesizing existing evidence on acupuncture in treating CTS.

pmc-12467847.title: From Cortex to Cardiac Response: tDCS of the Prefrontal Cortex Improves Autonomic Markers of Emotion Regulation
pmc-12467847.creator: Catarina Gomes Coelho, Jorge Leite, Raquel Pinto, Paulo P. P. Machado, Sandra Carvalho
pmc-12467847.description: Background: Emotion regulation (ER) plays a vital role in mental health, spanning mood, anxiety, and personality disorders. Cognitive reappraisal (CR) is one of the most common ER strategies and depends on prefrontal brain areas, but its success varies, and its neural basis is not fully clear.

pmc-12613473.title: CODABEILLES: a reliable reference library of COI DNA barcodes for French wild bees monitoring (Apoidea: Anthophila)
pmc-12613473.creator: Mélodie Ollivier, Anaïs Marquisseau, Eric Dufrêne, Rémi Rudelle, Rodolphe Rougerie, Adrien Perrard, Magalie Pichon, Emilie Andrieu, Emilie Andrieu, Emmanuelle Artige, Matthieu Aubert, Yvan Brugerolles, Alexandre Cornuel-Willermoz, Raphaël Da Silva Ropio, Adeline Dumet, David Genoud, Benoît Geslin, L
pmc-12613473.description: In the Anthropocene, the decline of insect pollinators poses a significant threat to ecosystem services, particularly to wild bee populations essential for plant biodiversity and agricultural productivity. France, with 983 species, hosts one of the most diverse bee faunas in Europe, yet these species face growing pressures from habitat loss, climate change, and intensive agriculture.

pmc-12807926.title: Bridging the gaps for women in substance use treatment
pmc-12807926.creator: Nancy Poole
pmc-12807926.description: This perspective provides an overview of a rapid review of research, and discussions held with Canadian treatment providers, that together illustrate how gaps persist in treatment and support for women with substance use concerns; and how attention to four elements of gender-specific treatment for women could ameliorate the situation.

pmc-13052749.title: Resting energy expenditure in professional dancers as an objective measure of low energy expenditure
pmc-13052749.creator: Matthew Wyon, Nick Allen, Derrick Brown-Appenzeller, Ross Cloak, Tracey Devonport, Kim Gregory, Joanne Penner, Zaki Hassan-Smith, Rachel Webster, Roger Wolman
pmc-13052749.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the prevalence of low resting energy expenditure (REE) in ballet dancers and to examine its association with low energy availability (LEA) questionnaires and physiological parameters, including menstrual function and body composition.MethodsParticipants were screened two times during a dance season. Measurements included direct REE (REEm) via gas analysis, body composition, bone health, menstrual status and LEA questionnaires.

pmc-13102772.title: Frequency shaping of tactile perception via transcutaneous interferential electrical stimulation: a simulation study
pmc-13102772.creator: Hiroki Ohara, Shunsuke Yoshimoto, Yasuyoshi Asai, Tomohiro Ota
pmc-13102772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrotactile feedback via transcutaneous interferential electrical stimulation generates temporally modulated stimulation fields and enables frequency-domain adjustment with carrier and beat frequencies. To systematically characterize these effects, we present a simulation framework that integrates tissue-scale electrical potential simulation with the finite element method and axon-scale dynamics using the axon cable equation, which incorporates cable theory and the Hodgkin–Huxley model, to predict axon activation and tactile perceptual metrics. We simulated a simplified glabrous skin model with three orthogonally oriented axons.

pmc-13231902.title: Cephalosporin use and patient outcomes following removal of penicillin–cephalosporin cross-reactivity alerts from the electronic health record
pmc-13231902.creator: Alicia Zimmer, Jessica Zagari, Paulina Sudnik, Alexandra Yamshchikov, Samia Lopa, Sarah Spitznogle, William DePasquale, Devin Donnelly, David Dobrzynski, Jessica Stern, Stephanie Shulder, Katelyn S. Quartuccio
pmc-13231902.description: Studies have shown there is minimal risk of cephalosporin cross-reactivity with penicillin (PCN), though avoidance in practice still occurs. Avoidance of cephalosporins due to reported PCN allergies can result in negative clinical outcomes. Removal of cross-reactivity alerts from the electronic health record (EHR) may increase cephalosporin utilization.

pmc-13649750.title: Rituximab with low-dose glucocorticoids for treating refractory membranous nephropathy: a prospective single-center cohort study
pmc-13649750.creator: Youqi Li, Yu Jiang, Wenwen Jiao, Jianwen Yu, Jianbo Li, Boxun Luo, Junbing He, Wei Chen, Qinghua Liu

pmc-13663185.title: Associations of Ginkgo biloba extract exposure with 12-month cognitive trajectories in amyloid PET–positive mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease: a pooled retrospective cohort study
pmc-13663185.creator: YoungSoon Yang, Yong Tae Kwak
pmc-13663185.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) show considerable heterogeneity in treatment response, underscoring the need for individualized therapeutic approaches. Ginkgo biloba extract is commonly used in cognitive disorders, but its efficacy in amyloid biomarker-confirmed populations remains unclear.

uslaw-usc-t43-s31d.title: 43 U.S.C. § 31d — Advisory committee
uslaw-usc-t43-s31d.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t43-s31d.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 2 (United States Geological Survey). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Establishment (1) In general There shall be established a 11-member geologic mapping advisory committee to advise the Director on planning and implementation of the geologic mapping program. (2) Members ex officio Federal agency members shall include the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency.
